scheduled_fire_needs.need: TRIGGER AND TIME: a trigger on trading weekdays, timed after the input's landing. One landing was measured: the Black Diamond silver partition dated 2026-10-13 was written 2026-10-14 at 11:46 UTC (one object read, LastModified). The 49 Financial trigger fires at 07:30 New York, which says nothing about this channel's landing; a Cottonwood time needs more than one landing measurement. The trigger input must name source blackdiamond_z09, because the handler passes the event's source to main.

IDENTITY AND GRANTS: the scheduled function's role (the 49 Financial holdings-performance role in holdings-performance/iam.tf) reads only the 49 Financial Schwab silver and writes only the 49 Financial gold prefixes. A blackdiamond_z09 fire therefore needs a Cottonwood principal that reads the Black Diamond silver prefix blackdiamond/cottonwood/silver/fact_holdings/ in opal-data-assets and writes the two Cottonwood gold prefixes, the per-firm principal pattern of the holdings refresh (directory/holdings_refresh.tf header item 1). No such principal appears in the served IAM list.

INPUTS CURRENT AT FIRE TIME: the Black Diamond silver prefix holds 93 date partitions from 2026-06-09, the newest 2026-10-13, which is T-1, so the input is 0 trading days behind T-1 (current, not stale). A fire on 2026-10-14 would find its input present.

CLOSE BASIS: the declaration holds partition_close OWN_DATE for this channel, inferred over the whole history (10 of 81 partitions were read at the cut). A fire that computes day t from partition t relies on that inference. The producer refuses a declaration that lacks partition_close.

METHOD AND DECLARATION VERSION: sources.json schema_version 1.2, which the producer requires (it refuses any other). The newest gold manifest (2026-09-25) carries schema_version 1.1 and the holdings-basis method with no inflow or outflow term. A fire writes at that method version.

PAIR OR HOLD: the fire writes served gold that the portal path reads (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/performance/holdings_gold.py), so creating the schedule is a LATER act under a never-widen pair (CLAUDE.md section 5). No pair for this channel is cited in this read, and this read changes nothing.

WHAT A FIRE WRITES: per trading date, two objects under the Cottonwood gold prefixes at opal_naming.address() output: holdings_performance_daily/date=D/data.parquet and holdings_performance_manifest/date=D/ (data.parquet and manifest.json), and only when run with --upload. The fire is served output, so it needs the later never-widen pair.

irpt_holdings_writer.who_writes: data/assets/scripts/gold/investor_reporting/holdings_snapshot.py writes irpt/<firm>/gold/holdings/date=D/<revision>.parquet. It runs per firm as holdings_snapshot.py --firms <firm> --upload on the daily-runner host, dispatched by infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/holdings_refresh/refresh_dispatch.py (one SSM command per firm) from the Lambda irpt-holdings-refresh-lambda. That Lambda is the target of the schedule irpt-holdings-snapshot (cron(15 10 ? * MON-FRI *), America/New_York), which reads State ENABLED on live describe. The Cottonwood holdings table is 3 trading days behind T-1: the ENABLED schedule has no partition for 2026-10-09, 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-13, and the cause is NOT_ESTABLISHED in this read (no run or SSM log read). The performance table has no trigger at all, so the contrast holds.
